title: first-light-autoscale-triage-and-kernel-todo (Rachel Nguyen)
content:
Goal: quick AM triage for the autoscale regressions and list kernel-level todos. This is a scratchpad — rough, tests to run, and handoff items.

Summary of current problem:
- Since ~2026-03-09 03:00 UTC we see spikes in p99 for small-request (<=64 tokens) paths when autoscaler spins up nodes. Spikes correlate with new workers hitting cold KVs and a sudden increase in microbatch flushes.
- Error rate stable; latency tail only during scale events. Observed on dedicated clusters in us-west-2 (tier: standard).

Immediate hypotheses:
1) Cold KV cache priming is causing long first-token latencies as kernels rebuild large KV pages on CUDA — investigate page fault / memcpy hotspots.
2) Autoscaler provisioning path sets kernel flags differently (missing --enable-shared-cache) in bootstrap userdata leading to per-request warmup.
3) Aggressive microbatch flush threshold combined with small batching yields serialization contention in batch scheduler.

Quick repro checklist (for oncall):
- Reproduce on dev cluster: run loadgen small-reqs (rps 1200, conc 50) while triggering scale-up (scale-managed set target+2). Capture traces.
- Commands: ./tools/loadgen --model=redwood-small --seq=64 --rps=1200 --concurrency=50 --duration=5m
- Capture: /api/trace?request_id=... and node-level nvidia-smi/stats, dmesg for CUDA mem events.

Kernel-level quick checks to instrument:
- Add temporary debug logging around KV cache populate (log when kv_populate starts/ends; sample every 10th request).
- Dump batch queue depth distribution at ms granularity (histogram).
- Verify startup flags: systemd unit and /etc/redwood/agent.conf on new nodes for --shared-cache and --kv-optimizations.

Experiments to run (ranked):
A) Flip shared cache on newly provisioned nodes and re-run load to confirm tail reduction (low risk).
B) Increase microbatch coalescing timeout from 2ms -> 6ms for small-req path to see effect on overall p99 (medium risk).
C) Add pre-warm job after node boot that performs a golden prefix run to populate KV pages (higher cost, schedule as canary).

Observations from quick local runs (03/11 AM):
- Local dev replicate: p50 ~12ms, p95 ~26ms, p99 ~210ms during scale spikes. Without scale: p99 ~42ms.
- When pre-warm script ran (300 warmup tokens) the p99 dropped to ~48ms during scale.

Actionable todos (me / immediate):
- [Rachel] Patch bootstrap userdata to include --enable-shared-cache, ship as canary image (infra PR). (owner: me)
- [Marco] Add KV populate debug logs behind debug flag and expose on /metrics-debug (owner: Marco).
- [Priya] Run controlled experiment on staging: A then B then C, record traces + cost delta. (owner: Priya)
- Create a short runbook entry for oncall: steps to mitigate (scale slower, enable shared cache, avoid simultaneous large model onboards).

Notes for followup meeting:
- Need to determine unit economics of pre-warming (CPU/GPU minutes vs saved tail cost). Tie to Optimize team.
- Consider autoscaler policy: prefer gradual ramp instead of sudden +2 nodes for bursty workload. Add to product backlog.

Open questions:
- Is the kernel code falling back to CPU memcpy during initial KV population on specific GPU driver versions? (check driver matrix)
- Are there any kernel-level locks that escalate during microbatch flush? (look at batch-scheduler spin-wait paths)

Log snippets (copied from trace):
- "kv_populate: start request=0x7f10abc, bytes=18MB"
- "batch_scheduler: flush took 8ms (queue_len=4)"
- "gpu-mem-copy: cudaMemcpyAsync stalled 4.8ms"

Quick links for triage:
- JIRA-INF-8421 (incident): https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-8421
- PR to change userdata: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/404
- Runtime PR (kv debug): github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/712

Handoff / if I get paged while OOO:
- Run 'stage-experiment A' (see runbook): deploy image with shared-cache flag and run loadgen for 10m. If p99 improves >50ms -> promote to canary in prod for 1h.
- If p99 not improved, revert image and run microbatch tweak B. Keep detailed notes in JIRA ticket.

Tiny todo list (personal):
- write short runbook paragraph (15-20m)
- open infra PR to ship userdata (30m)
- add KV debug logs PR (45m)
- schedule sync with Optimize + Autoscale (30m)

Random notes to self:
- Check which clusters still run driver 520.x vs 535.x — I think us-west-2 on dedicated is still 520. Might be relevant.
- Consider a small 'golden request' metric exposed in console: first-token-latency-after-boot.

End of sprint-scratch. Will convert to JIRA comments and runbook after sanity experiments.
